title: How to Make $1.6K/Day on Facebook Marketplace
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The guest owns How Equipment and invites viewers to buy a mower from him. The business results and margins are self-reported.

idea.name: Lawn and equipment dealership
idea.one_liner: Sell new and used lawn mowers and other equipment through a dealership, with service work as an additional revenue stream.
idea.customer: Buyers of lawn and other equipment.
idea.offer: New and used mowers and equipment, with dealership service capacity.
idea.revenue_model: Retail margins on equipment sales plus shop-rate service work.

key_quotes.quote: So, right now, who I am, I own an equipment dealership.
So, our best month, we did like 1.1 million last year

claims.claim: He said new zero-turn mower margins are 18–22% when the dealership is run well.
claims.quote: It's 18 to 22%. And that's that's if you're doing it right.

claims.claim: He said dealers who are not doing it right may make 10–15%.
claims.quote: You know, dealers that aren't doing it right, you're probably making more like 10 to 15%.

claims.claim: Some new zero-turn mowers sell for $12,000–$20,000.
claims.quote: I mean, they can get to like 12, 15, $20,000.

claims.claim: He described a used mower selling for about $5,000 against a new price of $15,000.
claims.quote: So you can have a used lawn or that sells for five grand and great value because they sell new for 15 grand, you know.

claims.claim: His shop rate is $125 per hour.
claims.quote: So the more hustle stuff like you'll find right now, what's my shop rate? It's $125 an hour.

claims.claim: He said the dealership's best month was about $1.1 million in sales.
claims.quote: So, our best month, we did like 1.1 million last year

claims.claim: Asked about net margin, he answered 20–25%; the transcript does not clarify the basis of that figure.
claims.quote: You know, we're 20 to 25.

claims.claim: He said sales make up 90% of his business.
claims.quote: So 90% of my business is sales.

claims.claim: He said a healthy dealership should have sales at about 60% of the business.
claims.quote: That's not a healthy dealership. You you should be like 60% sales.

claims.claim: He said good dealers can finish with 7–12% net margin.
claims.quote: So good dealers are walking away with like 7 to 12% net, you know, at the end of the tunnel.

claims.claim: He said the dealership became full-fledged four years after he bought the building.
claims.quote: I mean it's a full-fledged dealership at this point four years later.

claims.claim: He bought a side-by-side for $8,000 and listed it for $13,000 after it needed work.
claims.quote: And I bought it for 8,000, but this needed work. And I've got this listed for 13 grand right now.

claims.claim: He hoped to make a few thousand dollars on that side-by-side.
claims.quote: Probably hope to make a few grand on that.

claims.claim: He bought a Polaris Ranger for about $4,500–$5,000 and sold it for $10,000.
claims.quote: I bought it for maybe $4500, $5,000 and I sold it a few days ago for 10 grand.

claims.claim: He estimated his profit on that Ranger at about $4,000.
claims.quote: I probably made like four grand on that.

claims.claim: He bought another side-by-side for $3,750 and estimated its value at about $8,000.
claims.quote: I bought that for 3750. That one's probably worth eight grand.

acquisition_channels.details: Retail from the equipment dealership; he also says the business ships equipment to customers outside Michigan.

ideas.delivery: The dealership sells and services equipment from its store, with staff handling sales and mechanics handling service. It ships some purchases to buyers farther away.

prices: 10–15% for dealers not doing it right
20–25% stated in response to a net-margin question; basis unclear
$8,000 buy and $13,000 listing for a side-by-side
$4,500–$5,000 buy, $10,000 sale and about $4,000 stated profit for a Ranger

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to customer records; as a trader selling to consumers, the dealership would need to meet Consumer Rights Act obligations for new and used goods.

idea.name: Riding mower resale
idea.one_liner: Buy undervalued riding mowers and resell them near market value, mainly through Facebook Marketplace.
idea.customer: People looking to buy used riding mowers.
idea.offer: Used mowers bought below market value, preferably in ready-to-sell condition.
idea.revenue_model: Resale margin between the purchase and sale prices.

key_quotes.quote: Not flipping them, not fixing them up, just buying them undervalued and selling them at market value.
Start calling dealers and seeing what used equipment they have.
Find the dealers that are not advertising well.

claims.claim: The host introduced the guest with a claim of $50,000 profit in one month; the guest later described personal and partner earnings separately.
claims.quote: made $50,000 of profit in one month flipping riding mowers on Facebook Marketplace.

claims.claim: The guest said his first mower made a couple of dollars.
claims.quote: the first lawn mower I bought was right at the summer of, you know, a summer and I made a couple bucks on the zero turn.

claims.claim: The host stated that the first zero-turn made $100.
claims.quote: 100 bucks on your first zero turn.

claims.claim: The guest said he made close to $500 on the second mower.
claims.quote: The second one I made closer to 500.

claims.claim: He bought and sold 30 mowers that summer.
claims.quote: And that summer I bought and sold 30 of them.

claims.claim: He said he made $20,000–$30,000 profit that summer.
claims.quote: So I profited 20 to 30K that that summer.

claims.claim: He said his mower sales were usually quick, within a week.
claims.quote: within a week like every time it was it was quick.

claims.claim: He compared a 15% return on a $2,500 item with a 15% return on a $300 item.
claims.quote: So, I'm thinking in my head, 15% of 2500 bucks is a lot better than 15% of 300 bucks.

claims.claim: He said a driver could be paid $20–$25 per hour with his truck; the transcript renders the rate for a driver's own truck as “4 to $60.”
claims.quote: For me, the sweet spot is like 20 to $25 an hour if it's my it's literally like4 to $60 an hour if it's their truck.

claims.claim: He described a hypothetical pickup that could mean five hours in a car for a mower two hours away.
claims.quote: It's to sit in the car for 5 hours if this thing is 2 hours away.

claims.claim: He said he was spending eight hours a day in the car before hiring help.
claims.quote: I'm spending eight hours a day in the car

claims.claim: He bought about five to ten mowers himself before hiring a driver.
claims.quote: I bet it was like five to 10. It wasn't a crazy amount.

claims.claim: He said a mechanic was working about 20 hours a week for him.
claims.quote: I've got this guy like he's he's been doing like 20 hours a week for me at that point.

claims.claim: He estimated that mechanic's rate at about $14 per hour.
claims.quote: But he was probably working at like for he's probably like 14 bucks an hour.

claims.claim: He said he came to buy about 20–30 mowers per month from one dealer.
claims.quote: I got to the point where I was probably buying like, you know, 20 30 mowers a month just from this one guy.

claims.claim: He said there was room to make “a,000,” $2,000 or $2,500 on each mower; the first amount is unclear in the transcript.
claims.quote: And so that was a huge I mean and there's enough room for me to make a,000 $2,000 $2,500 on the mowers that he's Yeah.

claims.claim: He described a hypothetical deal where four or five contacts could be tried for a deal worth $1,000.
claims.quote: If I get four or five down the line and this deal is going to make a thousand bucks, you know, I I hate to ask it of my wife, but can I miss dinner tonight?

claims.claim: The host described another flipper selling 30 mowers in a month.
claims.quote: We sold a mower every day for the whole month. 30 mowers.

claims.claim: The host said that other flipper made $30,000 while working about 80 hours per week.
claims.quote: We made 30 grand. And that was like 80 hours a week of working.

acquisition_channels.details: Buy and sell through Facebook Marketplace; the transcript also describes Craigslist listings and Facebook groups for finding deals.
Call equipment dealers to ask about used inventory and build repeat sourcing relationships.
Visit dealers and estate or garage sales; hire drivers to collect equipment.

ideas.delivery: The founder finds and negotiates deals, then arranges inspection, pickup and resale. Drivers can handle long trips; the core approach avoids repair work where possible.

prices: $20–$25/hour driver rate with his truck; transcript says “4 to $60” for the driver's truck
About 20–30 mowers per month from one dealer

ideas.other_uk_rules: Screen outbound calls to businesses against CTPS and calls to sole traders against TPS. Apply UK GDPR to stored seller details and Consumer Rights Act obligations when trading used goods to consumers.

idea.name: Enclosed trailer resale

idea.customer: People looking to buy used enclosed trailers.
idea.offer: A used enclosed trailer sourced below market value.
idea.revenue_model: Resale margin between purchase and sale prices.

key_quotes.quote: was posted for $300.
That was my first trailer and I sold that for $3,000.

claims.quote: So, you can picture what an enclosed trailer >> Yep. >> was posted for $300.

claims.claim: He said he sold the trailer for $3,000.
claims.quote: That was my first trailer and I sold that for $3,000.

idea.offer: A house prepared for resale after a live-in flip.
idea.revenue_model: Resale proceeds above the purchase, holding and improvement costs.

key_quotes.quote: YouTube certified research on how to flip houses that I moved and was doing a live-in flip

ideas.delivery: The founder lives in the property during the flip; the transcript gives no further details about work performed or the sale.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Property transactions and personal data are subject to UK data protection and property law; the transcript gives no details about the transaction or improvements.

idea.name: Rent out a former home
idea.one_liner: Rent out a house after being unable to sell it, earning rental income instead of sale proceeds.
idea.offer: Use of the house as a rental home.
idea.revenue_model: Rental payments; amount and terms are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: And the house that I moved from, I ended up renting out instead of selling.

ideas.delivery: The owner rents out the house directly; tenant management and maintenance arrangements are not described.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to tenant records. Landlord duties, property safety requirements and any local licensing rules would apply; the transcript does not describe the location or arrangement.

idea.name: Family of Flippers
idea.one_liner: Teach trusted participants to flip mowers, provide equipment and setup, share some capital, and split deal profits.
idea.customer: People interested in learning mower flipping, including friends and contacts.
idea.offer: Instruction, equipment, setup and capital participation in mower-flipping deals.
idea.revenue_model: A profit share; the guest described a 50/50 split.

key_quotes.quote: I built a business called Family of Flippers.
So I would teach people, but it was kind of using some of my capital.

claims.claim: Participants and the guest each supplied half the capital; the guest also contributed equipment and setup.
claims.quote: We would use half of their money, half of mine. We would use my equipment, my setup, and I would get a certain percentage of that deal.

claims.claim: He described the split as 50/50.
claims.quote: And I think it was like a 50/50. So if they found a deal, I would still get 50% of the pie.

claims.claim: He said about five people did this alongside him.
claims.quote: We had like I had like five guys doing this alongside myself.

claims.claim: He said he personally made about $30,000–$35,000 from the deals he bought and sold.
claims.quote: Me personally, you know, this video that that you discovered me off of, me personally, the stuff I bought and sold was about like 30 to 35 grand that I made.

claims.claim: He said the other participants made about $15,000–$20,000; the transcript wording is unclear after that range.
claims.quote: And then there was like, you know, 15 to 20 grand made from like the 50s from the other people.

acquisition_channels.details: He recruited and taught former college basketball friends and other people he knew.

ideas.delivery: The founder teaches participants and contributes equipment and setup; participants also put in capital and find deals. The work involves handling and selling mowers.

prices: Half of deal capital from each side

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to participant records. If sold as a consumer coaching service, consumer contract and distance-selling rules may apply; DMCC subscription rules would matter if it were offered on a subscription basis.
